audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Draft translation aligned to Hebrew text; preserves prophetic letter and harsh outcomes. Needs witness-checks on prophetic-letter locus, place-name readings, and chronology.

verses.restored: Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.

familiar.text: Now Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.

notes.title: succession
notes.body: Formulaic royal notice; 'city of David' designates Jerusalem burial-place tradition.

verses.restored: And his brethren were the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah (variant), Michael, and Shephatiah; all these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

familiar.text: And he had brethren the sons of Jehoshaphat, Azariah, and Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Azariah, and Michael, and Shephatiah: all these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

verses.restored: Their father gave them great gifts of silver and gold and precious things, and fortified towns in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.

familiar.text: And their father gave them great gifts of silver, and of gold, and of precious things, with fenced cities in Judah: but the kingdom gave he to Jehoram; because he was the firstborn.

notes.title: gifts
notes.body: 'Gifts' (מַתָּנוֹת) likely denotes political/economic endowments; 'fortified towns' signals transfer of local power.

verses.restored: When Jehoram rose up to be king he strengthened himself and slew all his brothers with the sword, and also many of the princes of Israel.

familiar.text: Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Israel.

verses.restored: Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.restored: He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, like the house of Ahab; for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he did evil in the sight of YHWH.

familiar.text: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

notes.title: marriage
notes.body: Marriage to Ahab's daughter is a political-religious alliance that shapes policy and cult.

verses.restored: Yet YHWH would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that He had made with David, and as He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.

familiar.text: Howbeit the LORD would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever.

verses.restored: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and they set over themselves a king.

familiar.text: In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king.

verses.restored: Then Jehoram went forth with his princes and all his chariots; and he rose up by night and smote the Edomites that compassed him, and the captains of the chariots.

familiar.text: Then Jehoram went forth with his princes, and all his chariots with him: and he rose up by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him in, and the captains of the chariots.

verses.restored: So Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. At that time Libnah also revolted from under his hand, for he had forsaken YHWH, the God of his fathers.

familiar.text: So the Edomites revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. The same time also did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers.

verses.restored: Also he made high places in the mountains of Judah and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit whoring; he forced Judah thereto.

familiar.text: Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, and compelled Judah thereto.

notes.title: cultic language
notes.body: 'Whoring' (sexual language) denotes cultic idolatry and forced participation by the people.

verses.restored: And a writing came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, 'Thus says YHWH, God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,'

familiar.text: And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, Thus saith the LORD God of David thy father, Because thou hast not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

notes.title: prophecy
notes.body: The message attributed to Elijah appears in letter form—textual locus requires witness review.

verses.restored: 'But you have walked in the way of the kings of Israel and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a-whoring, like as the whoredoms of the house of Ahab; and you have slain your father's sons, who were better than you.'

familiar.text: But hast walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and hast made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and also hast slain thy brethren of thy father’s house, which were better than thyself:

verses.restored: 'Behold, YHWH will smite your people with a great plague, and with your children, and with your wives, and with all your goods.'

familiar.text: Behold, with a great plague will the LORD smite thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy goods:

verses.restored: 'You also shall have great sickness of your bowels, until your bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.'

familiar.text: And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.

verses.restored: And YHWH stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabians that were near the Cushites.

familiar.text: Moreover the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians:

notes.title: ethnic terms
notes.body: Hebrew names for groups preserved (Philistines, Arabians, Cushites); geographical relations imply southern/Negev alliances.

verses.restored: They came up into Judah and broke in and carried away all the substance found in the king's house, and his sons and his wives; and there was no son left him, save Jehoahaz the youngest of his sons.

familiar.text: And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

verses.restored: And after all this YHWH smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease.

familiar.text: And after all this the LORD smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease.

verses.restored: And it came to pass, at the end of two years, that his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness; so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him like the burning of his fathers.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that in process of time, after the end of two years, his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness: so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers.

verses.restored: Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign; and eight years did he reign in Jerusalem. He departed without being desired. They buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

familiar.text: Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years, and departed without being desired. Howbeit they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings.

translation_notes: Divine name יהוה rendered as YHWH throughout. Hebrew idioms (e.g., 'went a-whoring') preserved as cultic/sexual idolatry language. Proper names follow source spelling where relevant.
Where the Masoretic phrasing is compact or ambiguous (duplicate personal names, city-names), literal rendering preferred; variants flagged for later witness review.
safety_note: Contains descriptions of familial slaughter, forced cultic sexual acts, and violent conquest; these are preserved for accuracy, not endorsement.
